runner.text:
**Brief for the coach — Joe's program, 4–7 November 2026**

**What I did and why**

I compared the program Joe's old system ran (the Week A / Week B plan around the PT Tuesday) with the one in force now, looking for anything the new program had dropped. The clearest gap was direct biceps work. The old plan spread curls across Saturday pull (incline curls and hammer curls), Sunday push (dumbbell curls) and Monday pull (incline curls). The current program puts all of it on Sunday's deadlift day: Bicep Curl (Dumbbell) 3 sets of 8–12 and Hammer Curl (Dumbbell) 3 sets of 10–12, six sets in one session, plus whatever the PT adds on a chest-and-back Tuesday (estimated at 3 biceps sets, every other week). Joe's profile says direct biceps work is dumbbell curls, not barbell, and that is respected.

So I recorded an amendment: **Incline Curl (Dumbbell), 3 sets of 8–12 reps at RPE 8, 75 seconds rest, as the last exercise of Monday's OHP, back and arms session**, after the rear delt flys. Cues recorded: bench about 45°, arms hang straight down behind the torso, elbows stay back with a full stretch at the bottom, no shoulder swing. Progression is the usual double progression: add load once every set reaches 12. The stated reason on record is that direct biceps work was six sets in one session; an incline curl on Monday makes it nine over two days, at long muscle length, and keeps the lightest lifting day inside its cap.

**What was recorded**

- The program is now **version 4**, an amendment (not a redesign). It was adopted on 4 November 2026 with the hypertrophy emphasis unchanged and the rotation still starting at Week A. The training block that opened on 1 November **continues; it was not reset**.
- Monday's full session is now: Overhead Press (Barbell) — warm-up set of 5, warm-up set of 3, a top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4 back-off sets of 6 at 85% of the top set, 180 s rest; Chest Supported Row (Dumbbell) 4×8–12 at RPE 8, 120 s rest; Lateral Raise (Dumbbell) 3×12–15 and Rear Delt Fly (Dumbbell) 3×12–15 as a superset at RPE 8, 60 s rest; then the new Incline Curl 3×8–12 at RPE 8, 75 s rest. The kettlebell swing EMOM (12 minutes, 12 swings a minute at RPE 7 with the 40 lb bell, growing by 2 minutes to a cap of 16, reps up to 15) still sits beside Monday as its own session.
- Session time estimates against their caps: Monday **53 of 75 minutes** (it was the lightest lifting day and still is); Wednesday 39 of 75; Friday 65 of 75; Saturday 65 of 90; Sunday 65 of 90. Nothing is over.
- **No start load is recorded for the incline curl.** The engine will pick one when the next week's plan is drafted — from Joe's history if he has logged incline curls, otherwise it will need a weight chosen. Worth asking Joe what he last curled on an incline.
- Start loads the engine confirmed elsewhere, unchanged: Farmers Walk (Dumbbell) 50 lb per hand (45.4 kg) on Sunday; Kettlebell Swing 40 lb (18.1 kg) in both conditioning sessions.
- Nothing has changed in Hevy yet. Adoption changes the program on record; Joe's Hevy routines only change when the next week's plan is drafted and approved for pushing. The published pages and export were updated and committed; this week's page now reflects version 4. The store holds 1,130 logged sets, 147 exercises, 1 check-in, 5 milestones and 3 observations.

**What Joe must agree to**

1. Adding three sets of incline dumbbell curls to the end of Monday, 8–12 reps at RPE 8, with 75 seconds between sets. His Monday goes from about 48 to about 53 minutes. If he'd rather not, a further amendment removes it; nothing has been pushed to his phone.
2. A starting weight for it (see above).
3. How to handle the hand edits he's made in Hevy (next section): keep them on record as deliberate, or let the next push overwrite them.

**Warnings, and what each means**

*Three Hevy routines differ from the plan approved on 2 November.* Someone — presumably Joe — has edited routines in Hevy after they were pushed. The engine reports the differences by position, not by exercise name:

- One routine: the duration of exercise 1, set 2 was changed. (This looks like the daily dead hang, which is 2 sets of 20 seconds — but I can't confirm the name from what was returned.)
- A second routine: the reps on exercise 1, sets 5, 6 and 7, and the weight on exercise 2, sets 1, 2 and 3. This pattern fits Monday — the three back-off sets of the press and the first three sets of the row — but again the engine gave positions only.
- A third routine: the weight on exercise 3, sets 1–4; the duration on exercise 4, sets 1–2; and the weight on exercise 6, sets 1–3.

For training this is harmless in itself — the sets Joe logs are what count — but it means the routine he sees on his phone and the plan the engine thinks he's following have drifted, so next week's prescriptions may be built on the wrong assumption. It clears in one of two ways: record the edits as a deliberate override on the next week's plan (if Joe changed them on purpose, e.g. a weight that was wrong for him), or simply let the next push rewrite the routines from the plan. Ask Joe what he changed and whether he wants it kept.

*Deadlift weekly dose is 4 hard sets, below the 5–15 band for a maintenance phase.* The program's weekly targets for the priority lifts are bench 5, overhead press 5, back squat 5, deadlift 4, and 10 for the pull-up counting negatives and band pull-ups; the general target is 10 hard sets per muscle per week. Deadlift sits at 4 because Sunday plans exactly a top set of 5 at RPE 8 plus 3 back-off sets of 5 — four hard sets. This was already left in place on purpose with the reasoning that Friday's Romanian deadlift (3×6–10) carries the hinge pattern, the PT sometimes adds deadlifts on Tuesday, and a target of 5 would fire an under-target warning every week the session is done as written. For training: nothing changes; glutes, hamstrings and lower back also get Romanian deadlifts, hip thrusts (3×8–12) and swings. It would clear by adding a fourth back-off set and raising the target to 5, which I don't recommend while the block is new.

*The Friday strict pull-up single has no progression scheme, under a hypertrophy emphasis.* Friday opens with one strict pull-up attempt at RPE 10 as a test, held constant week to week. The engine expects every line to progress; this one deliberately doesn't. Also already acknowledged: the single is the weekly measure while Joe's max is 1; the negatives (3×2–4, lengthening the lower from 4–5 s to 6 s, then 8 s, then adding the vest) and the band pull-ups (4×5–8 on Wednesday and 3×5–8 on Sunday, moving to a lighter band at the top of the range) do the building. It clears once the test rep passes about five, when the strict line becomes real working sets with its own progression — which is exactly what Joe's profile asks for.

**Also worth knowing**

- The progress report has no weekly dose data yet — the block only opened on 1 November, so there is nothing to compare against targets until a full week closes.
- The deload rules in force: after at most 6 hard weeks, cut sets by 40%, keep loads, cap RPE at 8, and test the priority lifts.
- The Hevy pull that ran with the adoption (between 20:40 and 20:53 UTC on 4 November) found nothing new: no workouts, weigh-ins, routines or folders.

Published. Your training pages now show this week's program with the incline curl on Monday, and the block carries on as it was.

Two things before Monday:

**A starting weight for the incline curl.** I don't have a weight on record for you on this lift, so when I draft next week's plan I'll need one. What did you last curl on an incline? If you're unsure, I'd open with the same dumbbells you use for your regular curls minus a step, since the incline makes it harder at the bottom.

**Edits you've made on your phone.** Three of your routines in Hevy now differ from what I set on Sunday: a rest or hold time on the daily dead hang, and some reps and weights on what looks like Monday's press back-offs and row, plus weights and a hold time on one other day. The sets you log are what count, so nothing is lost. But when I draft next week I need to know whether to keep those changes or write over them. What did you change, and were they deliberate?

Nothing reaches your phone until you've approved next week's plan, so this coming Monday's routine in Hevy stays as it is. I'll put the incline curl in when we push the new week.
